emily: Thinking we should add a small runnable notebook that demonstrates batching + prefix caching + int8 quant profiles tradeoffs. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/489. Want feedback on scope and where to put it in the examples tree.

rafael: love this. customers keep asking for concrete numbers. keep the notebook <10 cells and have reproducible timings with a small toy model. where were you thinking to land it? examples/optimize/bench-demo.ipynb?

emily: yeah examples/optimize sounds right. I was planning a lightweight script cell that simulates requests and hits the hosted SDK client, but with env var to switch to a local mock if running offline. pseudo-code in PR: 

```python
# warm cache then run batched requests
client = OptimizeClient.from_env()
profile = {"quant": {"mode": "int8", "channelwise": True}}
client.deploy_profile("toy-model", profile)
# send 50 small requests and measure avg latency
latencies = []
for i in range(50):
    t0 = time.time()
    client.generate("toy-model", prompt="hello world", batch=4)
    latencies.append(time.time()-t0)
print('p50', np.percentile(latencies,50))
```

priya: small note: avoid actual deploy calls in the notebook for CI. prefer mocking the client or using a recorded trace. Also include a short section showing how cache warmup (prefix hits) changes the p95.

mark: agree with Priya. For CI we'll provide a minimal mocked results JSON and a test that asserts the notebook's rendered HTML contains the expected p50/p95 numbers. We already have a CI job for examples that runs nbconvert.

emily: great — plan: 1) add notebook with mock-mode flag, 2) add sample results JSON under examples/optimize/fixtures, 3) add simple pytest that converts notebook and checks strings. Will update PR.

rafael: can we also show a tiny snippet about batching vs cost? a line like: "Batch size X reduces per-token CPU time by ~Y% but may increase p95 for short requests" with an example table (2 rows) is enough.

priya: add a one-line caveat about quant + batch-size: for some hardware, int8 + large batch may push GEMM path that increases latency; link to perf playbook.

docs-bot: Build started for docs/pull/489 checks: nbconvert, linkcheck, lint

emily: i've pushed the notebook and fixtures. mock-mode uses MOCK_OPTIMIZE=1 env var and a small MockClient that reads results from fixtures/bench_results.json.

mark: ran nbconvert locally; one minor lint issue in a markdown cell (trailing spaces). i'll push a cleanup commit.

rafael: LGTM. one UX ask: include a tiny toggled cell at the top that sets VERBOSE=False so users can run the notebook quickly without printing per-request logs.

priya: can you also add a short paragraph under "Examples -> Optimize" in the sidebar linking to this notebook and noting it's runnable offline? small PR is fine.

emily: done — added sidebar entry and example blurb. docs-bot: re-run checks pls.

emily: awesome, will merge after the two small cleanup commits land. thanks all for the quick reviews! :rocket:
